title: NOVA: A Novel Vertex Management Architecture for Scalable Graph Processing
problem: Existing graph processing hardware accelerators require temporal graph partitioning to fit the working set into on-chip memory, limiting scalability to large graphs and causing bandwidth inefficiency from repeated DRAM accesses across partition sweeps.
motivation: Real-world graphs like social networks and web graphs have hundreds of millions of vertices and billions of edges that far exceed on-chip SRAM capacity; temporal partitioning imposes multiple DRAM passes over graph data, degrading performance and limiting scaling.
method: NOVA decouples reduction and propagation operations in the vertex-centric graph processing paradigm, allowing the entire working set to reside in off-chip DRAM rather than being partitioned across on-chip memory. On-chip memory is repurposed as a prefetch/access buffer to hide DRAM latency rather than as a traditional cache holding graph state. The design enables spatial tiling across multiple NOVA nodes for scale-out, achieving near-perfect weak and strong scaling. A cycle-accurate gem5-based model validates the architecture.
key_novelty: Decoupling reduction and propagation in the vertex-centric paradigm to eliminate the requirement for temporal graph partitioning, enabling direct DRAM-resident large-graph processing with latency-hiding on-chip buffers.
contributions: NOVA architecture decoupling reduction and propagation operations in vertex-centric graph processing, eliminating temporal partitioning.
On-chip memory used as DRAM-latency-hiding buffer rather than graph-state cache, enabling arbitrarily large graph processing.
Near-perfect weak and strong scaling via spatial multi-node tiling.
2.35x performance improvement over PolyGraph on synthetic graphs with 134M vertices and 2.14B edges using a fraction of PolyGraph's on-chip memory.
limitations: Evaluated primarily on synthetic graphs; real-world irregular graph topology effects on DRAM access patterns and buffer efficiency are not fully characterized.
primary_theme: Decoupled reduction-propagation vertex management for scalable large-graph hardware processing
